quote.translation: When Leibniz speaks, concerning contingent truths, of "detail without bounds" (détail sans bornes) and of "the infinite" (infinité) (Leibniz, Monadologie, 36), it is for the same reason.

regions.text: の理由からである。一つの交叉點の完全なる釋明は恐らく無限敷の交叉點の完全なる襷明を豫想するであらう。さうして無限数の交叉點の完全なる釋明っとは何等一つの交叉點をも残さない全き空康でなければならない。

quote.translation: The complete explanation of a single point of intersection would probably presuppose the complete explanation of an infinite number of points of intersection, and the complete explanation of an infinite number of points of intersection must be a total emptiness in which not a single point of intersection remains.

regions.text: 交叉點の偶然性がすべて主親に依存すると云ふならば、それは一切を主観化することに外ならないので、ちはや何ものる客觀性を有つたおのはないといふ結論に到達しなければならぬ。

quote.translation: To say that the contingency of points of intersection depends wholly on the subject is, in other words, to subjectivise everything, and we must then arrive at the conclusion that nothing any longer has objectivity.

regions.text: 我々は今迄と反對の立場に立つて見よう。交叉點の成立に關して出來るだけ偶然を除外して考へて見よう。

quote.translation: Let us now take up the standpoint opposite to the one we have held so far, and try to think about the formation of the point of intersection while excluding chance as far as we can.

regions.text: 丙點で甲と乙とが交又する場合例へば不連積線上の一點で甲の氣流と乙の氣流とが摺れ合つた場合または街上爽る地點で甲の男と乙の男とが出逢つた場合甲は甲を甲は甲を原因としこはこをではこを原因とし甲とごとがSを共通の原因にもつてあると考へよう。

quote.translation: Where A and B intersect at point C, for example where air current A and air current B rub against each other at a point on a line of discontinuity, or where man A and man B meet at a certain spot in the street, let us suppose that A has A′ as its cause and A′ has A″, that B has B′ as its cause and B′ has B″, and that A″ and B″ have S as their common cause.
In that case the Encounter (邂逅) of A and B cannot be called chance in the strict sense.
